venue_assessment.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Wide meat-free board (grain bowl, lentil soup, hummus sandwich, falafel wraps, stew), fresh and light, peanut-allergic deskmate orders freely, oat milk by default, olive oil instead of butter, white beans instead of cream. Meets everything: 3 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_slate_window: Satay dressing on every bowl and in-house roasted peanuts. Deal-breaker for Cyrus.
venue_assessment.downtown_wren_house: Every dish has meat or fish; vegetarian coworker left with only coffee. Deal-breaker for Mina.
venue_assessment.downtown_paper_kite: Light, peanut-free, half the board is meat-free, but cheese, cream, butter and whole milk everywhere. Roxy's intolerance costs a star: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.downtown_marble_steps: Peanut-safe, dairy-safe and meat-free breakfast plate, but heavy fried food that misses Brooke's wholesome request: 2 stars.

notes: Fair and solvable. Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, and the reviews make that clear. The allergy clue (emergency pen + satay) and the vegetarian clue (sushi day, zero meat) are indirect but backed up by Roxy's follow-up lines, so they are findable without being obvious. Marble Steps' vegetarian status is only shown through the breakfast plate, not the whole menu, but that doesn't matter because it already loses a star for being heavy. Linden Corner never says outright that it is dairy-free. You have to piece that together from oat-by-default, olive oil and white beans. That is fair, but a careful player might hesitate. Nothing contradictory.
